author: toketrain
body:
So there are a bunch of new Jr. Mods! That's awesome!
Unfortunately, I've now been in a few games in which there have been multiple Jr. Mods, all warning players about very small things. I understand that it must be exciting to be in this new position, but it's detrimental and, pardon my , it feels like they are all trying to outdo each other, like newly born turtles competing to swim to the ocean.

I think that if a staff member goes to a game, they should check if there's a staff member there already. If there is, the one that's there first should be punishing, and the other one should either leave or stay and enjoy the game.

replies.author: Lieutenantpants
replies.body:
This is my personal opinion. 
There is a difference between giving them a break and ridiculousness. Yes it's exciting to be a junior mod. Yes it's exciting to moderate the server for the first time. But the fact of the matter is that rules cannot be made up or stretched to allow junior moderators to deal more punishments. If I were a staff director, I would promote the guy who dealt 50 accurate punishments as was necessary and conducted himself well than the guy who dealt 300 and spent most of his/her time trying to outdo everyone else. 27 is a ridiculous amount of Juniors, whether that's good or bad is open to debate, but if there are going to be 27 then things are going to have to run a little differently.

replies.body:
My opinion, please respect it.
Having 27 Junior mods works out fine because of the following reasons.
1. Soon the Juniors will relax a after a while and shall become more slack when it comes to warnings, etc. Spock, I agree with what you said about the Junior Mods trying to outdo each other, so hopefully everyone will relax a bit.
2. I'm sure many of the Juniors are spread around the world so because of the time zone differences, not everyone is going to be on at the exact same time. 
3. Some of the Juniors may have things going on in life which will cause them to be away from Avicus for a short period in the future so I'm sure there will be times where Avicus shall lack in staff. E.g. School exams, vacation, etc.

replies.author: Mooch24
replies.body:
Teamspeak: Juniors aren't able to handle and resolve issues on TS very well. They tend to spam the kick command and punish players prematurely. 

In-game: Extremely robotic. Over 1/2 the jr's don't even know the proper punishments and how to dish them out properly. It's the first few days and I don't think people expect much differently. But they're chosen for a reason. They should fix all and any issues within the first 2-3 days of receiving the position. Any longer and they aren't quite ready yet.

Forums: It's just ridiculous. They're trying to act all serious and make informative posts that end up having little to no correlation to the OP or question(s) asked. Some are extremely inactive and can't seem to find a proper time and place to create a post or thread due to not having solid connections with the majority of members. They seem to not take criticism very well.
 
I do understand that the first few days or week can be tough. It's a lot of new responsibilities put on your plate and there's so many things you need to handle at once. But, If you're not capable of handling these things after being exposed for an extended period of time, you're not cut out for the position.
